thread:
Maya S: FYI - customer (tenant: tenant_7b5) reports repeated 429s + latency spikes since ~06:12 UTC. Route: /v1/generate, model: redwood-base-13b-q4. They provided a sample request id r-7b5-9f3a. Any quick triage steps?
Jared O: I'm looking. Can you paste the full request-id and any response headers they saw?
Maya S: Req-id r-7b5-9f3a, short excerpt from their response: 429 Too Many Requests, headers: 
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 167890
Retry-After: 30
```
They say it started after a batch job kicked off from their side.
Olga R: That header set looks like tenant-level quota exhaustion (remaining=0). Two quick checks: per-tenant token burn in the spike window, and whether the route was included in any recent rollout that changed model/seq length.
Maya S: I grabbed some logs: we see a burst of long-sequence requests from tenant_7b5 between 06:11:40-06:13:12, peak throughput ~220r/s.
Eli T: tagging what I queried: 
```
index=api-requests tenant=tenant_7b5 route=/v1/generate | stats count, sum(tokens) by model, bin(_time, 1m)
```
Shows majority tokens on redwood-base-13b-q4 and many requests with seq_len>4096.
Rachel P: From product POV, that workload definitely climbs token consumption fast. Is that a single job? If so we should suggest client-side batching limits.
Jared O: Can someone confirm whether tenant_7b5 has a reserved capacity contract? If not, they're on shared hosted quotas (burst-limited).
Maya S: Customer says they're on hosted pay-as-you-go. No reserved capacity.
Olga R: Ok that explains it. For observability/attribution: we need to show them the per-tenant 5m token burn chart and the per-route 429 heatmap. I recommend these quick artifacts: 1) timeline of token/s request rate 2) 429s by route+model 3) sample request traces for a few req-ids.
Jared O: Actionable repro steps we asked the customer to run (so support has a repro): 
1) Re-run their batch with single-threaded caller and capture headers.
2) Take one representative payload and run: 
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-base-13b-q4","input":"<their large prompt>","max_tokens":2048}'
```
Look for X-RateLimit-* headers and Retry-After.
Maya S: They ran that curl and got Retry-After: 30 consistently.
Eli T: For attribution we also need to verify whether the system applied route-based throttles vs tenant quotas. Query we used: 
```
select count(*) as errs, sum(tokens) as tokens from api_events where tenant='tenant_7b5' and _time>=06:10 and _time<=06:15 group by error_type, route, model
```
That shows errors sharply tied to that route/model combo.
Olga R: Ops note: we have two quota layers: rate-limits (req/s) and token quotas (per-minute windows). When token quotas hit, X-RateLimit-Remaining goes 0 and 429s are returned. Route-level quotas can also be set for some enterprise tenants.
Rachel P: Can support provide the customer with a short doc explaining how to detect if it's a tenant quota vs route quota? We can add a small sample dashboard link.
Maya S: Draft reply to customer: "Looks like a token quota exhaustion caused by an internal batch job generating long sequences. Immediate mitigations: lower max_tokens, add client-side throttling, or switch to Dedicated if sustained. We're attaching our token burn + 429 timeline."
Jared O: I'll create a short-lived alert: tenant_7b5 429s > 30 in 5m -> notify support on-call. Also adding a dashboard panel filterable by tenant to the limits dashboard (per-tenant token rate, 429 heatmap, model breakdown).
Olga R: For long-term observability improvement: add these panels to Defaults: - per-tenant token burn (1m/5m), - 429 attribution by route/model, - per-tenant rolling quota headroom. Also add a drilldown on req-id to link to full trace.
Eli T: FYI deploy-bot shows a scale event we had at 06:10 UTC: "autoscaler increased pool by 20 GPUs" — not related but good to note.
DeployBot: autoscaler: scaled dedicated-pool-prod from 80 -> 100 at 06:10:05 UTC (trigger: cpu>70%)
Maya S: Customer accepted mitigations for now and will throttle their job to stay under peak. We've shared the logs and dashboards.
Rachel P: Follow-up item: consider a UX nudge in console when a tenant sees repeated 429s pointing them to upgrade to Dedicated or enabling client-side throttles. Filing a small ticket.
Jared O: Closing loop — created support ticket #SUP-3129 with artifacts and recommended next steps. If the customer sees repeated bursts after applying throttles, escalate to account team for Dedicated sizing conversation. :thumbsup:
Maya S: Thanks all, marking resolved for now.
